title: The I2C Communication Bus
summary: Network dozens of sensors and displays using only two wires: SDA and SCL! Master addresses and bus scanning.

steps.title: Why Buses Save Wires
steps.markdownContent: If every sensor, display, clock, and keypad required dedicated pins, an Arduino Uno would run out of pins after adding 3 devices. With the **I2C** (Inter-Integrated Circuit) bus, up to 127 unique peripheral devices share the exact same two wires without interfering with each other!

steps.title: SDA, SCL, and 7-Bit Hex Addresses
steps.markdownContent:
The I2C bus uses two open-drain signal lines:

- **SDA (Serial Data)**: Transfers data bytes bidirectionally (on Pin `A4`).
- **SCL (Serial Clock)**: Synchronizing clock ticks generated by the Controller (on Pin `A5`).
- **7-Bit Hex Address**: Every module has a unique address (e.g. `0x27` for LCDs, `0x68` for Real Time Clocks). The Uno broadcasts the address before transmitting data, and only the matching chip responds with an ACK bit!

steps.title: Parallel Bus Breadboard Wiring
steps.markdownContent:
Wire the 16x2 LCD (`comp_07`) and DS3231 RTC (`comp_10`) in parallel:
1. Connect both module `VCC` pins to Uno `5V`.
2. Connect both module `GND` pins to Uno `GND`.
3. Connect BOTH module `SDA` pins to Uno Pin `A4`.
4. Connect BOTH module `SCL` pins to Uno Pin `A5`.
